chapters.author: Leo Tolstoy (Poem: Mildred Bowers Armstrong)
learning_outcomes: Learn the philosophical wisdom that the most important time is 'now', the most important person is the one you are with, and the most important affair is to do good.
Appreciate the subtle observation of nature in the poem 'The Squirrel'.
Understand reported speech, phrasal verbs, and dictionary usage.
summary_points: A king seeks answers to three questions: What is the right time to begin something? Who are the right people to listen to? What is the most important thing to do?
A wise hermit helps him realize the answers practically by nursing an injured enemy who had come to assassinate the king.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why did the king want to know the answers to three questions?
How did the king and the hermit nurse the wounded man and save his life?
Match the items in List A with their meanings in List B: (a) Wounded, (b) Awake, (c) Forgive, (d) Faithful.
Imagine you are the king. Write a diary entry describing your meeting with the hermit in the forest and the lessons you learned.

chapters.author: Vasantha Surya (Poem: D.J. Enright)
learning_outcomes: Understand empathy, compassion towards destitute people, and innocent generosity of children.
Enjoy the humorous contrast of adolescent non-conformism in the poem 'The Rebel'.
summary_points: Mridu visits her aunt Rukku Manni's house in Chennai where children find a kitten hidden in the backyard.
Seeing a poor beggar with blistered feet on the hot road, the children generously give away the music master's old slippers.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What made Mridu conclude that the beggar had no money to buy chappals?
What did the rebel do when everybody had short hair according to the poem?
Fill in the blanks with the correct form of the words given in brackets: (scrawny, vanished, peering).
Write a short paragraph on why acts of kindness towards animals and needy people make the world a better place.

chapters.author: Comic Folk Tale (Poem: Frank Flynn)
learning_outcomes: Appreciate comic strip storytelling with speech bubbles and witty humour.
Overcome irrational fears through curiosity as highlighted in the poem 'The Shed'.
summary_points: The king challenges witty courtier Gopal to buy a huge Hilsa fish and bring it to the palace without anyone asking a word about the fish.
Gopal smears ash on his face, wears rags, and behaves like a madman so that everyone talks about his appearance rather than the fish, winning the challenge.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What was the challenge given by the king to Gopal regarding the Hilsa fish?
How did Gopal prove that nothing is impossible when one applies intelligence and wit?
Change the following direct speech dialogues into indirect speech: Gopal said, 'I accept the challenge, Your Majesty.'

chapters.title_en: The Ashes That Made Trees Bloom
chapters.author: William Elliot Griffis (Poem: Michael Rosen)
learning_outcomes: Appreciate Japanese folklore celebrating honest, kind-hearted people and fidelity of pets.
Understand how adult instructions ('Chivvy') affect growing children.
summary_points: A kind old Japanese couple loved their pet dog Muko, who led them to buried gold.
Greedy neighbours killed the dog, but the dog's spirit appeared in dreams directing them to make a mortar and spread magical ashes that made withered cherry trees bloom.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: How did the spirit of the dog help the good old couple the second time?
Why did the daimyo reward the good old man but punish the greedy neighbour severely?
Write a story on the theme 'Greed leads to ruin whereas kindness earns lasting rewards.'

chapters.author: John Galsworthy (Poem: Shirley Bauer)
learning_outcomes: Appreciate devotion, passion, and uncompromising craftsmanship over mass commercialization.
Recognize the ecological and life-giving importance of trees celebrated in Shirley Bauer's poem.
summary_points: German bootmaker Mr. Gessler made bespoke boots of exquisite leather and everlasting quality in London.
Despite losing business to big industrial firms advertising inferior shoes, he refused to compromise on quality till his dying breath.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What was Mr. Gessler's complaint against the big shoe manufacturing firms?
Why did the author consider bootmaking an art in the hands of Mr. Gessler?
Use the following words in meaningful sentences of your own: (a) Splendid, (b) Contempt, (c) Starvation.

chapters.author: Sharada Dwivedi (Poem: Maude Rubin)
learning_outcomes: Develop analytical reasoning, deduction, and avoid jumping to hasty judgments.
Enjoy the playful personification of a noisy ceiling fan in 'Mystery of the Talking Fan'.
summary_points: Ten-year-old Maya and her seven-year-old brother Nishad (Seven) investigate mysterious tenant Mr. Nath living at their mother's clinic.
Maya suspects him to be a crook on the run, while sympathetic Nishad believes he is a poor, lonely, and starving invalid needing a friend.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What did Nishad find out about Mr. Nath from Ramesh, the boy who served him meals?
Why did Maya prepare a list of facts about Mr. Nath?
Whose perspective do you agree with more — Maya's suspicious mind or Nishad's compassionate attitude? Give reasons.

chapters.author: Roald Dahl (Poems: Kit Wright, Muriel L. Sonne)
learning_outcomes: Enjoy science fantasy, humorous exaggerations, and playful inventive language.
Understand how harmless garden snakes help control insect pests as described in 'Garden Snake'.
summary_points: Inventor Willy Wonka invents 'Vita-Wonk' to make people older after Wonka-Vite made people so young they vanished into negative ages.
He travels the globe in the Great Glass Elevator collecting samples from the oldest living trees, animals, and reptiles to concoct an age-increasing elixir.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why did Mr. Willy Wonka decide to invent Vita-Wonk?
Name three of the oldest living things that Mr. Wonka collected ingredients from.
Add suitable prefixes (un-, in-, dis-) to make antonyms of: (a) Possible, (b) Patient, (c) Agree, (d) Efficient.

chapters.title_en: A Homage to our Brave Soldiers
chapters.author: Department of Military Affairs (Poem: Lois Brandt Phillips)
learning_outcomes: Inculcate deep patriotism, respect, and gratitude towards armed forces defending national frontiers.
Discover delightful wonders of meadow ecology depicted in 'Meadow Surprises'.
summary_points: Children visit the National War Memorial in New Delhi, observing the Amar Jawan Jyoti and four concentric chakras: Amar Chakra, Veerta Chakra, Tyag Chakra, and Raksha Chakra.
They learn about highest gallantry awards like the Param Vir Chakra (PVC) awarded to brave martyrs such as Major Somnath Sharma and Captain Vikram Batra.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What are the four concentric chakras of the National War Memorial in New Delhi?
What is the highest wartime gallantry award in India? Who was its first recipient?
Write a letter of gratitude to an Indian soldier posted at the Siachen Glacier thanking them for safeguarding our freedom.

chapters.title_en: The Tiny Teacher & Bringing Up Kari
chapters.author: Supplementary Reader: Dhan Gopal Mukerji
learning_outcomes: Learn lessons of discipline, hard work, mutual cooperation, and duty from the life of ants.
Understand animal behaviour, empathy, and bonds of companionship between humans and elephants.
summary_points: The Tiny Teacher shows the ant's remarkable communal life where no ant ever quarrels or shirks responsibility in the anthill.
Bringing Up Kari narrates the endearing adventures of a mischievous baby elephant who saves a drowning boy from a river.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why is the tiny ant called the wisest and most hardworking teacher for mankind?
How did Kari save the drowning boy from the river?
Write three moral qualities that human beings can learn from ants.

chapters.title_en: Stories of Courage & An Alien Hand
chapters.title_te: ధైర్య సాహస కథలు మరియు గ్రహాంతర హస్తం
chapters.author: Supplementary Reader: Rudyard Kipling, Zakir Husain, Axel Munthe, Jayant Narlikar
learning_outcomes: Understand freedom, courage, and respect for wild animals.
Explore science fiction depicting subterranean planetary civilization and interplanetary exploration.
summary_points: Chandni, Abbu Khan's little goat, chose freedom on the hills and fought a wolf bravely until death rather than living in captivity.
In 'An Alien Hand', Tilloo lives in an underground city on Mars and accidentally deactivates an unmanned exploratory rover sent from Earth by pressing the red button.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why did Chandni refuse to join the herd of goats and prefer to fight the fierce wolf on the hills?
What happened when Tilloo pressed the red button on the control panel in 'An Alien Hand'?
Write a science fiction narrative imagining how human astronauts will interact with subterranean creatures upon landing on Mars.
